report.source_text: Investigations on admission showed a white cell count of 0.79×109/L, with neutrophils 0.56×109/L. Following admission, she was started on daily filgrastim due to her neutropaenia and low CD34+ count, which precluded successful mobilisation. C-reactive protein (CRP) was elevated at 74, and procalcitonin was 0.18. Blood cultures and a blood fungal culture were negative.

report.source_text: A punch biopsy of the nodule confirmed lobular panniculitis with an inflammatory cell infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, mixed with lymphocytes, eosinophils, histiocytes and occasional multinucleated giant cells (figure 2A). Granulomas were not observed. No features of vasculitis were identified. Gram-positive cocci were present in the dermis and subcutis (figure 2B). No fungal organisms or acid-fast bacilli were seen on Grocott’s methenamine silver or Ziehl-Neelsen stains. Culture from the punch biopsy grew MRSA.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A female in her 20s with relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma presented with fever and bilateral tender, indurated subcutaneous nodules over her shins. Initial investigations showed neutropenia and elevated CRP, but negative blood cultures. An ultrasound of the nodules showed increased echogenicity and vascularity without abscess. A punch biopsy of a nodule confirmed lobular panniculitis with Gram-positive cocci, and culture grew MRSA. The patient was treated with doxycycline, leading to resolution of fever and nodules.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with fever and bilateral scattered tender, indurated subcutaneous nodules over shins with mild overlying erythema, approximately 3–5 cm in diameter.
Initial investigations showed neutropenia (WBC 0.79×10^9/L, neutrophils 0.56×10^9/L) and elevated C-reactive protein (74), with negative blood cultures.
An ultrasound scan of the leg nodule showed vague increased echogenicity and increased vascularity in the subcutaneous tissue with no evidence of abscess formation.
A punch biopsy of the nodule confirmed lobular panniculitis with an inflammatory cell infiltrate and Gram-positive cocci in the dermis and subcutis.
Culture from the punch biopsy grew MRSA.
Treatment with doxycycline resulted in resolution of her fever and nodules.

No features of vasculitis were identified on biopsy (E004).
Ultrasound showed no evidence of abscess formation (E003).
